attempts.raw_response: The answer probably lies in recognizing that the earliest Gospel was not treated as a fixed literary text but as a living tradition, continually adapted to the needs of different communities. Mark's Gospel, on this view, is not a slavish copy of something earlier but a stabilized form of preaching and teaching that had circulated orally and in fragmentary written form before being committed to a single continuous narrative. The variations we might expect are not those of one author copying another's manuscript, but rather the natural differences arising when oral tradition crystallizes into written form. This does not solve every difficulty, but it relieves the pressure of supposing a vanished predecessor nearly identical to Mark yet somehow distinct. The primitive document, in short, may simply be Mark itself in its earliest redaction.

pair.human_continuation:
If he had simply copied or
reproduced it without change, that would have been intelligible;
if he had added freely to it, that also would have been
intelligible: but, as it is, he seems to have put in a touch here
and made an erasure there on principles that it is difficult for
us now to follow. We are indeed here at the very _crux_ of
Synoptic criticism.

For our present purpose however it is not necessary that the
question should be solved. We have already obtained an answer on
the two points raised by Papias. The second Gospel _is_
written in order; it is _not_ an original document. These two
characteristics make it improbable that it is in its present shape
the document to which Papias alludes.
pair.prefix:
The theory that we have in the
second Gospel one of the primitive Synoptic documents is not
tenable.

No doubt this is an embarrassing result. The question is easy to
ask and difficult to answer--If our St. Mark does not represent
the original form of the document, what does represent it? The
original document, if not quite like our Mark, must have been very
nearly like it; but how did any writer come to reproduce a
previous work with so little variation?

source_document.title: The Gospels in the Second Century by William Sanday
